Markdown began as a way to write for the web without writing HTML. It was never
given a grammar, only a description and a script, and every tool since has had
to decide for itself what the description meant.

That is *why* two tools can disagree about the same file. One reads an indented
line as code; another reads it as the end of a list. Neither is wrong, because
nothing says which is right.

> A format with no grammar is a format with as many grammars as it has readers.

The rest of this essay is about living with that.
